o1.biggest_strength: Every move has a sized projection with a named assumption, and the numbers check out: Lite is 70% of churners, the multi-site free accounts bring 42% of free-tier conversions, and Advanced customers leaving for Semrush are only about 9 per 10,000 a month.
o1.biggest_mistake: I asked for moves ranked by impact, but it ranks them by quickest money and puts the agency report last. That undersells the one place Semrush actually beats us. It also never puts a date on the data, and our voice says every claim has a number and a date.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Rank by impact as asked, or argue the order more strongly. Date the data. Tie the multi-site free-account onboarding track directly to the agency report so the two moves work together.

o2.biggest_strength: It makes the agency report the focused bet and refuses PPC parity. It links the multi-site free-account track to that report and calls Lite our biggest leak, backed by sharp numbers: 37% of Lite customers remain after a year, and usage limits cause about a third of all churn. It also says plainly what not to do, including cutting prices for creators.
o2.biggest_mistake: Move 5, the content studies, is the generic 'do more content' idea with a thin success measure and no projection. The enterprise move also has no sized projection, unlike the others.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace or sharpen Move 5, add a projection for the enterprise pack, and say why Lite sits second rather than first even though it is the cheapest, fastest money.

reason: Both are sharp and their numbers hold up. The second ranks by impact as I asked, makes agency reporting the clear bet and connects the moves to each other. The first sizes its projections a bit more rigorously but buries the reporting move last.
